subject.title: Production scaling: relaxing the single-writer session lock for multi-user deployments

question: After current main's stale-lane repair is production-verified, should OpenClaw preserve serialized mutation per canonical session or design a new concurrent same-session state model?
rationale: Reader/writer locking, prioritized batching, and session pools introduce new ordering, context-sharing, persistence, and compatibility contracts that cannot be selected from the incident logs alone.

options.title: Preserve serialized sessions
options.body: Keep one writer per canonical session, use existing sharding, and fix only reproducible lifecycle gaps in the focused bug tracker.

options.title: Sponsor concurrency design
options.body: Keep this issue as an architecture tracker and define ordering, isolation, persistence, and upgrade contracts before implementation.

recommendation.title: Preserve serialized sessions
recommendation.body: Keep one writer per canonical session, use existing sharding, and fix only reproducible lifecycle gaps in the focused bug tracker.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest cross-cutting history on reply lifecycle and stale-lane recovery policy, making him the best available owner for the architectural choice.
